:::{#def-right-hand-limit}
#### Right-hand limit

Let $f$ be a function and $L$ a real number.
The **right-hand limit** of $f$ at $c$ is $L$
[@wikipedia_one_sided_limit],
written $\lim_{x \to c^+} f(x) = L$,
if for every $\tolout > 0$ there is a $\tolin > 0$ such that
$\abs{f(x) - L} < \tolout$ for every $x$ with $c < x < c + \tolin$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-left-hand-limit}
#### Left-hand limit

Let $f$ be a function and $L$ a real number.
The **left-hand limit** of $f$ at $c$ is $L$
[@wikipedia_one_sided_limit],
written $\lim_{x \to c^-} f(x) = L$,
if for every $\tolout > 0$ there is a $\tolin > 0$ such that
$\abs{f(x) - L} < \tolout$ for every $x$ with $c - \tolin < x < c$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-one-sided-limit}
#### One-sided limits

Let $f$ be a function.
The right-hand limit (@def-right-hand-limit) and the left-hand limit (@def-left-hand-limit) of $f$ at $c$
are the **one-sided limits** of $f$ at $c$.

:::
